source_1_quote: The UK's average petrol car produces 164 grams of CO2 per kilometre equivalent (g CO2e), while a diesel car produces 170 grams of CO2/km.
source_2_quote: The carbon footprint of travel is measured in grams of carbon dioxide-equivalents per passenger kilometer.
calculation_notes: Average petrol car 164g/km minus cycling 16g/km (metabolic emissions)

source_1_quote: The UK's average petrol car produces 164 grams of CO2 per kilometre, equivalent (g CO2e)
source_2_quote: Average car CO2 conversion factors published annually
calculation_notes: Walking has near-zero direct emissions. Full car savings

source_1_quote: An urban bus emits 104 g/km and a coach 27 g/km due to its greater weight efficiency.
source_2_quote: Bus emission factors vary by type - local bus approximately 100g CO2e/pkm
calculation_notes: Average car 164g/km minus bus 104g/km = 60g saved

source_1_name: UK Office of Rail and Road
source_1_quote: Passenger train emissions per passenger kilometre was 31 grams of CO2e. This was down 2% on the previous year.
source_2_quote: DEFRA has an emission factor for an average National Rail journey of 0.03546 kgCO₂e per passenger km.
calculation_notes: Average car 164g/km minus national rail 31g/km = 133g saved

source_1_quote: Eurostar, emitting only 6 g/km per passenger on trips through the Channel Tunnel.
source_2_quote: The 2019 estimates were 6.0 g CO2e per passenger km for international rail (Eurostar).
calculation_notes: Eurostar emits only 6g/km. Car 164g - 6g = 158g saved

calculation_notes: Short-haul flight 251g/km vs train 35g/km. At 500km including RF multiplier

source_1_quote: For every 1,000 tons of food waste landfilled, an estimated 34 metric tons of fugitive methane emissions are released.
source_2_quote: For each metric ton of food waste that goes into a landfill you get about 0.86 tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e) released to the atmosphere as methane.
calculation_notes: EPA 2023: 0.86 tonnes CO2e per metric ton of food waste = 860g/kg

action_name: Composting food scraps instead of landfill
source_1_quote: 1 kg CH4 per dry ton materials * 23 kg CO2 per kg CH4 = 23 kg CO2 (well-managed compost) vs 207 kg CO2 (poorly managed).
source_2_quote: EPA research indicates that diverting food waste from landfill reduces the methane generation potential by 33%.
calculation_notes: Composting emits ~10-20% of landfill methane. Net savings ~700g/kg

source_1_quote: Recycling a single can saves 1.56 megajoules (MJ) of energy or 98.7 grams of CO2 equivalent.
source_2_quote: The primary energy demand for recycled aluminium was 8.3 gigajoules per tonne, resulting in a significant energy saving (95.5%).
calculation_notes: Recycling saves 95% energy vs virgin aluminum. Per 15g can saves ~99g

source_1_quote: Recycling PET saves significant energy compared to virgin production
source_2_quote: According to EPA, recycling aluminum saves 95%, paper 60%, glass 30% of energy.
calculation_notes: 500ml PET bottle weighs 28g. Recycling saves ~1.7kg CO2/kg plastic

action_name: Using LED instead of incandescent bulb
source_1_quote: LEDs use up to 90% less energy and last up to 25 times longer than traditional incandescent bulbs.
source_2_quote: A single 10-watt LED will save about 800 kWh over its lifetime. That single replacement will eliminate emissions of 1000 pounds of carbon dioxide.
calculation_notes: 60W incandescent vs 10W LED = 50W saved. At US grid 0.37kg/kWh = 18.5g/hour

action_name: Air drying clothes instead of tumble dryer
source_1_quote: Tumble dryers are energy-intensive appliances using 4-5 kWh per cycle.
source_2_quote: Heating and drying processes are among most energy-intensive household activities
calculation_notes: Tumble dryer uses ~4.5 kWh/load. At US grid = 1.67kg CO2

action_name: Cold water laundry instead of hot
source_1_quote: Washing at 30°C instead of 40°C can save around 40% of the energy per wash cycle.
calculation_notes: Hot wash uses ~1.6 kWh more than cold = 592g at US grid

source_1_quote: 89kg CO2 ÷ (25.7l × 0.59sw/p/d × 365d ÷ 7l/min) = 0.1154 kg CO2 per min
source_2_quote: Reduce an estimated 359 kg CO2-e emissions per annum. Assumes 9 L/min flow rate.
calculation_notes: 7L/min flow, heating water from 13°C to 55°C = ~115g CO2/min

action_name: Reusable shopping bag instead of plastic
source_1_quote: Cotton bags need 7,100-20,000 uses to break even. Polypropylene bags break even in 10-45 uses.
source_2_quote: HDPE bags have lower environmental impacts than paper or cotton when used once
calculation_notes: Plastic bag ~10-33g CO2. After breakeven, each use saves full amount

action_name: Reusable water bottle instead of single-use
source_1_quote: Single-use plastic bottles have significant lifecycle emissions from production and transport
calculation_notes: 500ml PET bottle ~83g CO2e. Reusable breaks even in 10-30 uses

action_name: Buying secondhand clothing instead of new
source_1_quote: Extending the life of clothes by just nine months reduces carbon, water and waste footprints by around 20-30% each.
calculation_notes: Average new garment ~13kg CO2e avoided

source_1_quote: Urban trees sequester 85-140 lbs CO2 over first 10 years
calculation_notes: Trees absorb 10-40kg CO2/year. Conservative 15kg/year estimate
